PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 03/14/28 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, persistent lower extremity edema, and mental health evaluation.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately five weeks after his last visit. He reports that his respiratory symptoms have remained stable, with no significant exacerbations. He continues to use his albuterol inhaler three to four times daily, particularly during episodes of exertion or exposure to cold. He notes occasional wheezing, especially in the early morning hours, but denies any episodes of dyspnea at rest or nocturnal awakenings.
Mr. Fairfax expresses continued concern regarding his persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, which has not improved despite adherence to dietary sodium restrictions and ongoing furosemide therapy. He describes the edema as worsening with prolonged standing and reports increased discomfort, which he rates as 6/10 on a pain scale. He has been diligent in monitoring his fluid intake and has not experienced any signs of shortness of breath or chest pain.
In terms of mental health, Mr. Fairfax reports that while he has continued to practice mindfulness, he has experienced an increase in anxiety levels over the past month. He describes feeling overwhelmed by recent life changes, including the passing of a close friend. His sleep has been more disrupted, with increased episodes of waking in the night feeling anxious.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + increased fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + dyspnea on exertion, + intermittent wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using three to four times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 120 mg daily (consider increasing). 7. Sertraline 100 mg daily.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.4F, HR 76, BP 128/78, RR 20, O2 sat 82% on room air.
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but engaged. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 4+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.9, Hgb 10.5, Hct 30.8, Plt 210. 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.1, Cl 101, CO2 28, BUN 36, Cr 2.2, Glucose 90. 3. BNP: 620 (stable). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory symptoms remain stable; however, the slight increase in wheezing may warrant a reassessment of inhaler technique. Continue albuterol as needed and maintain the current tiotropium dose. A follow-up pulmonary function test is recommended in one month to assess lung function. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema has worsened, and an increase in furosemide dosage to 160 mg daily is recommended. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and monitor weight daily. A follow-up with nephrology is advised to reassess renal function and diuretic therapy. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax reports increased anxiety levels. Consider increasing sertraline to 150 mg daily to better manage symptoms. Schedule follow-up with psychiatry in two weeks for ongoing management and reassessment of treatment efficacy. Explore additional therapeutic options such as cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) to address anxiety.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
